video_title: How Jesse Pollak Is Mapping Out Base's Next Chapter After the App Pivot
gist: Jesse Pollak tells Laura Shin why Base's on-chain social/creator-coin bet failed and why he is handing the Base app to Jordan 'Kobe' Fish to refocus on Base-the-chain as financial infrastructure, addresses the Brian Armstrong meme-coin PFP controversy, responds to Robinhood Chain's rapid user/fee growth, and details concrete Base roadmap metrics -- new tech-stack upgrades, a B20 tokenization standard targeting 20,000 TPS, a new enterprise privacy product, and Base's dominant share of agentic-payment transaction volume.

themes.theme: Base's strategic reset: handing the app to Kobe

insights.claim: Jesse Pollak publicly acknowledged that Base's social and creator-coin bet at the app level 'didn't work out' and announced he is handing day-to-day leadership of the Base app to Jordan Fish ('Kobe') so he can refocus his own time on Base as core financial infrastructure.
insights.speaker: Jesse Pollak
insights.so_what: A concrete leadership and roadmap-reallocation signal at one of the largest L2 ecosystems -- watch for the Base app to pivot hard toward trading/prediction-market/perps products under new leadership.
insights.quote: some of the things that we had tried didn't work out the way that we had expected or hoped

insights.claim: Jesse Pollak frames the app-level failure as a matter of strategic mistiming rather than a wrong long-term thesis: he still believes crypto will eventually consume all of society including social, but argues that finance-adjacent categories (stablecoins, tokenization, prediction markets, perps) are where real product-market fit exists today, and that Base underinvested there while chasing social.
insights.speaker: Jesse Pollak
insights.so_what: Signals Base's forward roadmap will concentrate almost entirely on finance-native products (trading, tokenization, payments) rather than social/content-coin features for the foreseeable future.
insights.quote: if you look at kind of where crypto is getting product market fit today, it's really infinite... stable coins, tokenization, prediction markets, per uh these uh categories are growing incredibly quickly

insights.claim: Jesse Pollak states that Base the chain (distinct from the failed app-level social bet) has become the largest on-chain spot market in the world for crypto trading -- Bitcoin, Ethereum, and other assets reportedly trade more on Base than on any other chain -- and one of the world's most important stablecoin settlement rails, built up over the last two years largely outside public attention.
insights.speaker: Jesse Pollak
insights.so_what: A specific, checkable claim of category leadership (largest on-chain spot market) that investors evaluating L2/chain market share should verify and monitor against competing chains.
insights.quote: it's it's now the biggest spot market in the world for crypto trading on chain

insights.claim: Jesse Pollak cites his personal trust and working relationship with Jordan Fish ('Kobe') -- whom he says he was directly involved in recruiting to Coinbase -- as the deciding factor in handing him the Base app and a broader Coinbase-wide trading-product mandate, describing the split as a 'natural partnership' between chain-infrastructure focus (his) and trading-product focus (Kobe's).
insights.speaker: Jesse Pollak
insights.so_what: Clarifies the internal Coinbase/Base leadership structure and mandate split going forward, relevant to tracking accountability for Base app trading-product execution.
insights.quote: there's no one there's no one better than him to do that

themes.theme: The Brian Armstrong meme-coin PFP episode

insights.claim: Per Laura Shin's framing, a memecoin called 'Brian' (not launched or endorsed by Brian Armstrong) rallied roughly 37x to about a $37 million market cap after Armstrong changed his X profile picture to an affiliated image, then crashed about 90% a couple of days later after Armstrong swapped his PFP to a CryptoPunk image -- prompting Armstrong to publicly disclaim his account as a source of investment signals.
insights.speaker: Laura Shin
insights.so_what: A concrete, quantified case study of the outsized, fast-moving market impact a single executive's social-media activity can have on an unaffiliated token -- relevant to assessing reputational/market risk whenever public figures interact casually with speculative assets.
insights.quote: it ended up doing like 37x up to about a $37 million market cap, but then a couple days later he swapped it for a Cryptounk and then the token crashed about 90%

insights.claim: Jesse Pollak defends Brian Armstrong's PFP change as consistent with Armstrong 'saying what he means and meaning what he says' -- i.e., a genuine expression of excitement about CryptoPunks and Coinbase, not an implicit endorsement -- and argues Base/Coinbase's position is that Armstrong's personal social posts should never be treated as trading signals.
insights.speaker: Jesse Pollak
insights.so_what: Shows Base/Coinbase leadership's official messaging line on executive social-media risk -- useful for gauging how the company will likely respond to similar incidents in the future (defending intent rather than restricting behavior).
insights.quote: you shouldn't be trading Brian's PFP as a core piece of financial advice

insights.claim: Jesse Pollak argues the deeper structural problem with meme coins and creator coins is a mismatch between short-term trading drama and the long-term-oriented incentive design that successful crypto assets need -- coins like 'Brian' were never created or endorsed by their namesake and had no long-term structure, making the resulting drama 'unsurprising' rather than a market failure to fix.
insights.speaker: Jesse Pollak
insights.so_what: Signals Base's product philosophy going forward will emphasize long-term-incentive-aligned asset design over pure speculative/creator-coin mechanics, relevant to what kinds of tokenized assets Base will prioritize supporting.
insights.quote: the thing that you want is you want things that are oriented towards the long term that have the right incentives to to be set up for the long term

themes.theme: Competitive pressure from Robinhood Chain and new entrants

insights.claim: Per Artemis data cited by Laura Shin, Robinhood Chain -- launched only a few weeks before this interview -- had already surpassed Base in daily active users by roughly 2x, and its 24-hour fees were already roughly 4x Base's, illustrating how quickly a well-distributed new entrant can outpace an incumbent L2 on raw activity metrics.
insights.speaker: Laura Shin
insights.so_what: A sharp, specific competitive data point for anyone tracking L2/chain market-share dynamics -- incumbency and multi-year infrastructure investment did not prevent a fast-launching, well-distributed rival from quickly overtaking Base on DAUs and fee volume.
insights.quote: it's actually already surpass base in terms of the number of daily active users twice... 24-hour fees on Robin Hood chain have already like roughly 4xed the same on base

insights.claim: Jesse Pollak acknowledges that new entrants like Robinhood Chain and Stripe's Tempo have a real distribution advantage for the current wave of non-crypto-native users being onboarded, since Base's existing edge (deep integration into every centralized exchange, Coinbase's tens of millions of funded accounts) is strongest among users who are already crypto-native rather than traditional-finance customers.
insights.speaker: Jesse Pollak
insights.so_what: An unusually candid admission of a genuine competitive gap from an incumbent L2 founder -- worth weighing against Base's stated distribution-based counter-strategy when assessing relative competitive positioning.

insights.claim: Jesse Pollak's counter-strategy against new entrants leans on Coinbase's brand, existing ETF/institutional relationships, and an increasingly mature developer platform (payments, wallets, trading infrastructure) as the distribution lever for onboarding the next wave of non-crypto customers, rather than competing purely on short-term activity or incentive metrics.
insights.speaker: Jesse Pollak
insights.so_what: Clarifies Base's actual competitive playbook against Robinhood Chain, Tempo, and similar entrants: institutional/brand distribution and developer-platform maturity rather than a race on raw usage metrics.

insights.claim: Jesse Pollak states that crypto adoption overall remains extremely early, with less than 1% of the world currently using the technology, framing current inter-chain competition (Base vs. Robinhood Chain vs. others) as fighting over a still-tiny slice of a rapidly growing total pie rather than a zero-sum contest.
insights.speaker: Jesse Pollak
insights.so_what: Useful framing for investors weighing competitive-share losses at any single chain against the much larger total addressable market still to be captured industry-wide.
insights.quote: less than 1% of the world is using this technology

themes.theme: Base's technical roadmap: network upgrades and throughput

insights.claim: Base has moved off a third-party Optimism-based OP stack onto its own dedicated technology stack over the last six months, and is now shipping major upgrades (Azul, then Barrel, then Cobalt coming around late August/September) on a roughly six-to-twelve-week cadence rather than the prior close-to-annual upgrade cycle.
insights.speaker: Jesse Pollak
insights.so_what: Signals materially faster protocol iteration speed for Base going forward, relevant to assessing its ability to keep pace technically with faster-moving new entrants like Robinhood Chain.
insights.quote: we're trying to get on a pretty fast cadence here where we're not waiting a year for an upgrade but instead upgrades are shipping every kind of like six to 12 weeks

insights.claim: Base's new 'B20' tokenization standard, introduced with the Barrel upgrade, is designed to give stablecoin and tokenized-equity issuers compliance and privacy controls out of the box, and Jesse Pollak states it will push Base's throughput from roughly 6,000-7,000 transactions per second pre-B20 to a targeted 20,000 TPS by the end of the year or possibly by the end of the current quarter.
insights.speaker: Jesse Pollak
insights.so_what: A specific, trackable technical performance target (20,000 TPS) that can be used as a concrete benchmark for evaluating Base's execution against its own stated roadmap.
insights.quote: right now it's more like 6 to 7,000 transactions a second that we could do preB20... we can do uh, 20,000 transactions per second uh, by the end of the the year

insights.claim: Base has already processed roughly $150 million of trading volume in B20-standard assets since the standard's introduction, which Jesse Pollak cites as early evidence of high-quality traction for the new tokenization standard.
insights.speaker: Jesse Pollak
insights.so_what: An early, quantifiable adoption metric for a brand-new tokenization standard, useful for tracking growth trajectory in subsequent quarters.
insights.quote: with B20s, I think we've already done something like $150 million of volume

insights.claim: The upcoming 'Cobalt' upgrade focuses on native-account improvements -- paying gas in any stablecoin, fewer transaction approval steps, easier key rotation, and better multisig controls -- framed by Jesse Pollak as a developer-experience improvement intended to flow through into better consumer-facing account UX.
insights.speaker: Jesse Pollak
insights.so_what: Gives a concrete preview of near-term account-abstraction/UX improvements coming to Base, relevant to assessing whether onboarding friction for non-crypto-native users will meaningfully improve.
insights.quote: they can pay for gas in any uh stable coin. Um they can uh not have to have do do multiple approvals. It's easier to do key rotation.

themes.theme: Agentic payments and enterprise privacy (Base Ledgers)

insights.claim: Jesse Pollak states Base already processes roughly 90% of all transactions on the agentic-payments protocol (referred to in the conversation as 'x42'/x402), driven largely by stablecoin payments for AI use cases such as paying for data, inference, video generation, and automated sales outreach, with both transaction counts and volume rising week over week.
insights.speaker: Jesse Pollak
insights.so_what: A striking, highly specific market-share data point (roughly 90% of agentic-payment transaction volume) positioning Base as the dominant settlement layer for the emerging AI-agent payments category -- a concrete lead to monitor as agentic commerce scales.
insights.quote: X42 today base does something like 90% of all the transactions

insights.claim: Base launched 'Base Ledgers,' an enterprise privacy product, about a month before this interview, letting enterprises transact privately on-chain while retaining full compliance controls and access to Base's existing DeFi liquidity rather than having to build their own; Jesse Pollak reports 'really strong demand' from enterprises reluctant to expose customer data on a fully public chain.
insights.speaker: Jesse Pollak
insights.so_what: Identifies a specific new enterprise on-ramp product (privacy plus compliance plus DeFi liquidity access) that could be a meaningful driver of institutional adoption on Base, worth tracking for disclosed enterprise wins or volume.
insights.quote: it basically lets enterprises do transactions uh that are private um while kind of retaining full compliance controls for them

themes.theme: Base ecosystem signals and cross-chain philosophy

insights.claim: Jesse Pollak points to Morpho's rapid growth in lending/financing, plus newer projects like Banker and Virtuals (tokenization and creator-business infrastructure) and Umeia (a token model incorporating longer-term prediction-market-based governance), as evidence the underlying Base builder ecosystem is thriving independent of the app-level social setback.
insights.speaker: Jesse Pollak
insights.so_what: Suggests the core DeFi/financing layer of the Base ecosystem remains healthy and growing even as the consumer-app-level social strategy failed, relevant to separating infrastructure-layer health from app-layer execution when evaluating Base overall.

insights.claim: Jesse Pollak frames Base's philosophy as being 'a bridge, not an island' -- supporting EVM chains, Solana, Bitcoin, and now even integrating rival Robinhood Chain within the Base app -- prioritizing a seamless cross-chain user and developer experience over exclusivity to the Base chain itself, even for a product literally named 'the Base app.'
insights.speaker: Jesse Pollak
insights.so_what: A notable strategic choice -- deliberately integrating a direct competitor chain into its own flagship app -- that signals Base is optimizing for aggregator-style distribution and trading volume capture over chain-level tribalism.
insights.quote: we want Bass to be a bridge on an island
